machines.name: KIM-1
machines.rights: The monitor ROM is MOS Technology's, copyright 1975, and MOS was bought by Commodore in 1976; who holds it now was not established, and no licence or permission from any holder was found. Our copy is Hans Otten's dump of real 6530-002 and 6530-003 chips, kept in this repository under roms/, with where it came from, and checked by SHA-256 each time it is read.
machines.notes: The keypad, the six LED digits, the RS and ST keys, the SST switch and both 6530s, with the original monitor ROM. Not modelled: the teletype interface, the cassette interface and the expansion bus.

machines.name: Synertek SYM-1 (first sold as the VIM-1)
BBC Micro
machines.rights: The three ROMs are Acorn's: the operating system, MOS 1.20, BBC BASIC 2 and the Disc Filing System, DFS 1.20. The operating system's own text says copyright 1981 Acorn Computers Ltd. and BASIC's copyright 1982 Acorn. Who holds that copyright now was not established, and no licence or permission from any holder was found. Our copies are from jsbeeb's ROM folder at a pinned commit, kept in this repository under roms/, with where they came from, and checked by SHA-256 each time they are read. The position is documented, not cleared: if a rights holder asks, the ROMs will be removed.
machines.notes: The keyboard, the picture in all eight screen modes, teletext included, the sound chip, and the disc drive with Acorn's DFS, on MOS 1.20 and BBC BASIC 2. Not modelled: the serial port, the analogue port, the Tube, the cassette interface, the printer port and the 1 MHz bus.

photos.author: simon.inns
photos.caption: an original Acorn BBC Micro Model B
photos.alt: An original Acorn BBC Micro Model B seen from the front left and slightly above on a blue cloth: a beige case with a black keyboard panel, a row of ten red function keys along the top, the "British Broadcasting Corporation Microcomputer System" badge above them, and three indicator lights for cassette motor, caps lock and shift lock below the bottom left of the keyboard, to the left of the space bar.
photos.used: the photograph of the machine at the head of its page; nothing is traced or measured from it, because the BBC Micro has no 3D model

machines.name: NES
machines.rights: The NES has no system ROM: the console runs whatever cartridge is in it. Commercial games are not bundled and never will be: load your own, which is read in this tab and not uploaded. The cartridge Start puts in is Lan Master, a puzzle game by Shiru from 2011, which he released into the public domain in his own words, in its manual: "It is free of charge, released into Public Domain, and provided "as is", without warranty or responsibility of any kind." Its title screen says PD2011 Shiru. Our copy is the 2015 build, with rainwarrior's fix, from Shiru's own archive, lan_master.zip, as the Internet Archive kept it: https://web.archive.org/web/20160327132502id_/http://shiru.untergrund.net/files/nes/lan_master.zip, SHA-256 79410cc133f1100d2fe5409fd49297a62afc748aeeb5faccb8fe69c68c16e6aa, because his own site's files could not be fetched on 6 October 2026. It is kept in this repository under roms/, with where it came from, and checked by SHA-256 each time it is read.
machines.notes: The picture drawn a dot at a time as the PPU draws it, the sound unit's five channels, two controllers, NTSC and PAL, and six cartridge boards: NROM, MMC1, UxROM, CNROM, AxROM and MMC3. Not modelled: the Dendy, the Famicom Disk System, expansion audio, the Zapper and other peripherals, the unlicensed mappers, the analogue quirks of the picture, and saving battery-backed RAM.
